selected.name: Explanatory mechanism depth
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the work explains why a phenomenon occurs using a coherent mechanism, theory, or diagnostic analysis; give 0 when it mainly reports a method and aggregate empirical gains without explanation.
selected.rationale: R05, R20, R21, and R45 investigate underlying representation, robustness, or training dynamics rather than only introducing a technique.
member_names: Explains causal mechanism, not just reports outcome
Mechanistic hypothesis that is itself put at risk

selected.name: Structure-matched inductive bias
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the representation or architecture encodes a real structural property of the domain and the abstract explains why that structure matters; give 0 when the architecture is generic or structurally unmotivated.
selected.rationale: R12 uses higher-order attention for logic, R51 uses hyperbolic geometry for hierarchies, and R59 uses finite-element structure for physical dynamics.

selected.name: Causal intervention quality
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the study changes targeted factors or uses counterfactual controls to distinguish competing mechanisms; score 0 when it merely correlates observations with outcomes or compares opaque systems.
selected.rationale: R04 contrasts labels with blurred inputs and auxiliary tasks, while R15 intervenes on clean/adversarial normalization and network depth.

selected.name: Failure-mode-to-mechanism fit
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract identifies a specific bottleneck and gives an intervention whose mechanism directly addresses it; score 0 when the method is generic or disconnected from the stated problem.
selected.rationale: R07 links mobile skills to compounding navigation errors, while R42 links behavior priors to conflicting offline data sources.

selected.name: Simplifying conceptual payoff
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the work removes unnecessary components, stages, or learned machinery while preserving the intended function and explaining why; score 0 when it only adds complexity.
selected.rationale: R28 reduces diffusion-based representation learning to a much simpler denoising formulation, while R48 simplifies a multi-stage long-tail method into one training stage.

selected.name: Counter-Intuitive Scientific Finding
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract highlights a surprising or paradoxical phenomenon that challenges conventional wisdom (e.g., 'removing clean images boosts robustness'). Score 0 if the results are exactly what one would expect from standard methods.
selected.rationale: The dense model rewards the identification of deep paradoxes or surprising insights (R55, R33), indicating high scientific value that rigid scorecards fail to capture.
member_names: States a genuinely surprising, precisely contrasted finding

selected.name: Explains an existing phenomenon vs. names a new system
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract's primary contribution is characterizing/explaining an already-observed phenomenon versus introducing a new named architecture, model, or system as the headline deliverable. A 10 is a pure analysis/characterization paper with no new named system. A 0 leads with a new named model/system as the headline contribution.
selected.rationale: R30 (dense_pct=0.959, 'Phenomenology of Double Descent') and R49 (dense_pct=0.807, 'The Early Phase of Neural Network Training') are pure characterization papers introducing no new named system, both dense-favored; R06 (card_pct=0.946, InfinityGAN) and R20 (card_pct=0.789, SELF-PARAM) each lead with a new named system as the headline, and both score far higher on the scorecard than on the dense model.
member_names: Explains an existing phenomenon vs. names a new system
Primary contribution is understanding, not a new benchmark artifact

selected.name: Novel Core Architectural Primitive
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract introduces a completely new mathematical operation or topological structure at the core of a neural network (e.g., higher-dimensional attention, novel tensor products). Score 0 if it uses standard architectures with only external modules or hyperparameter tweaks.
selected.rationale: The dense model strongly credits structural innovations to a network's core mathematical operations (R01, R33), which a scorecard might underweight compared to standard task performance.

selected.name: Actionable interpretability
selected.instruction: Give 10 when analysis exposes internal structure that supports prediction, intervention, control, or a substantive scientific explanation and validates that use; give 0 when interpretability is only visualization or post hoc labeling.
selected.rationale: R23 derives controllable hidden-state directions, R59 links learned components to physical dynamics, and R42 uses compositional prototypes to explain user interests.

selected.name: Recasts the problem in a formal frame that buys leverage
selected.instruction: Score whether a known problem is restated inside a different, precisely named formal frame, and whether the reframing purchases something concrete. 10: the abstract names the reformulation (an optimisation problem, transport between distributions, an extension of a classical theorem, an information-theoretic quantity) AND names what it yields -- a derivation, an explicit formula, a near-optimality statement, a bound, a new estimator. 5: a reformulation is announced but nothing specific follows from it. 0: the problem is stated in its standard form and attacked with the standard toolkit for that form.
selected.rationale: R41 turns ad hoc use of a learned model into an explicit optimisation and derives near-optimal algorithms from it; R55 reframes docking as transport between distributions and gets unbalanced flow matching; R52 extends Gauss-Markov by permitting bounded bias and derives closed-form estimators; R31 imports rate-distortion estimation to general sources and derives two-sided bounds. This reframing move produces no new benchmark and no new dataset, so it is invisible to criteria keyed on artifacts or wins.
member_names: Recasts the problem in a formal frame that buys leverage

selected.name: Something survives when all benchmark numbers are deleted
selected.instruction: Mentally strike every leaderboard number, percentage and speedup from the abstract and score what remains. 10: a substantive claim remains standing -- a mechanism, a limit, a phenomenon, a design principle -- that a reader could carry into other work; the numbers were evidence for it rather than the content of it. 5: a modest transferable claim remains alongside numbers that do most of the work. 0: what remains is only 'we propose X and it performs better than baselines'; the numbers were the claim.
selected.rationale: Strip the numbers from R26 (+4.1 AP), R47 (40 percent smaller at 0.5 percent drop), R48 (76 minutes) and R38 (92.7 versus 28.5 ASR) and the residue is largely 'our variant wins'. Strip them from R01 and the two-domain hypothesis and the depth demand survive; from R18 the claim that most modern components are inessential survives; from R05 the argument about label uncertainty survives. A scorecard with items for empirical strength and margin size will grade quantified deltas generously, which is the clearest over-crediting direction in this slice.
member_names: Something survives when all benchmark numbers are deleted

selected.name: Rigorous Bounds vs Heuristic Trade-offs
selected.instruction: 0 = discovers an empirical, ad-hoc trade-off between two conflicting metrics. 10 = mathematically establishes rigorous bounds, optimal trade-offs, or fundamental optimality conditions.
selected.rationale: R29, R40, and R60 establish optimal mathematical bounds, explaining the dense model's preference, while R41 and R42 merely describe an empirical trade-off between conflicting metrics.

selected.name: Abstract Word Count
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the abstract is exceptionally long or wordy, from 0 (very short/concise) to 10 (excessively long/verbose). Do not judge the quality of the writing, only the sheer volume of text.
selected.rationale: Text length often biases automated evaluation models independent of the core insight. The dense model might favor highly concise abstracts (e.g., R34 is very brief), while the scorecard model might score longer, more detailed abstracts higher simply because they contain more checkable words (e.g., R60 is exceptionally long).
member_names: Abstract bulk: length, sentence count, paragraph count

selected.name: Math Notation Density
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the abstract contains dense mathematical notation, LaTeX formatting, variables, and formal definitions, from 0 (none) to 10 (very dense). Do not judge the correctness of the math, only its visible presence.
selected.rationale: Theoretical sub-fields have different norms that leave a heavy fingerprint of inline math. R40 uses matrix notation ($A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$), and R59 discusses RKHS and Gaussian universality. A scorecard model might blindly award points for this apparent rigor, while a dense text model might penalize the low readability.
upstream_parent_all_members: author's mathematical communication and disciplinary style

selected.name: Branded system or acronym naming
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the abstract coins or foregrounds a catchy system name or acronym (e.g., “ImpScore”, “Point-SAM”, “VariBAD”, “ProtoSnap”). Score 0 for no coined name, 10 for multiple emphasized branded names. Do not judge whether naming is effective; score only how much branding is present.
selected.rationale: Catchy names can make an entry seem more established than it is. R03 (Point-SAM) and R30 (VariBAD) both push a branded name into the title and abstract, a surface signal a dense model may overweight while a scorecard ignores it.
upstream_parent_all_members: author's practice in the format / marketing

selected.name: Public-release and link boilerplate (code, data, project page)
selected.instruction: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the text contains explicit availability or release statements: full URLs (GitHub repositories, project pages, university or lab sites, shortened links), and phrases such as 'code is available', 'publicly available', 'we release', 'our data and code can be found at', 'model weights are public', 'see our project page'. 0 = no availability statement and no URL anywhere; 5 = a bare availability phrase with no location; 10 = multiple release statements and one or more full URLs, prominently placed. Score only the presence, count and prominence of release/availability language. You must NOT judge whether releasing artifacts is good practice, whether the release seems credible or complete, whether the work looks reproducible, or whether the hosting location seems reputable.
selected.rationale: A pasted URL is a single cheap token that any criterion bank can reward, yet it reflects whether a group has spare engineering hands and a habit of shipping, not what was discovered. The asymmetry across the two arms of this slice is stark: nearly every dense_low_card_high item carries a link or a release sentence (R01, R02, R13, R15, R17, R25, R33, R46, R54, R55), while the most extreme dense_high_card_low items carry neither (R21, R53, R07, R50, R38, R60). Tagged mixed because groups with the capacity to release code plausibly also do more careful work, so the discount should be reported as a band rather than assumed to be pure nuisance.
member_names: Public-release and link boilerplate (code, data, project page)
selected.upstream_parent: the producing group's release norms and its engineering or staffing capacity to package artifacts
upstream_parent_all_members: author's/lab's standing habit of open-sourcing artifacts (a submission norm shaped by lab culture or subfield convention, not by the idea itself)
the producing group's release norms and its engineering or staffing capacity to package artifacts

selected.name: Surface polish and typographic perfection
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the abstract is free of typos, grammatical errors, and formatting quirks, exhibiting a uniformly professional copyedited style. Score 0 for many errors, 10 for flawless polish. Do not judge whether polish makes the paper better; score only how clean the text is.
selected.rationale: A polished surface can make an entry read as higher quality than its substance warrants. R04 and R42 are both typographically immaculate and smoothly phrased, the kind of finish that may bias a dense reader while adding nothing to the research content.

selected.name: Defensive Consensus Challenging
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the abstract uses explicit phrasing to claim it is challenging a consensus, debunking an open secret, or resolving a widespread misconception, from 0 to 10. Do not judge if the consensus is real.
selected.rationale: Authors sometimes manufacture a 'strawman' consensus to elevate their work's perceived importance. R35 explicitly states 'This consensus, however, is challenged in this paper', and R45 begins by naming an 'open secret in contemporary machine learning'. This is a rhetorical framing tactic that can artificially inflate relevance.
member_names: Rhetorical challenge to a stated prior consensus
upstream_parent_all_members: position in the run of the field — this framing is only available to an entry written after a prior 'obvious' consensus view has already been staked out and named by others

selected.name: Contemporary LLM/agent-era vocabulary density
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate how much of the abstract's vocabulary belongs to the current large-language-model/agent wave (terms like 'large language models', 'hallucination', 'context-faithfulness', 'agents', 'in-context', 'proactive', 'self-updatable') as opposed to classical statistical/ML-theory vocabulary. 0 = no such terms present; 10 = the abstract is saturated with this vocabulary. Score only the density of this topical vocabulary, not whether the topic choice itself is a good or important one.
selected.rationale: R32 is built entirely around 'large language models', 'hallucinations', and 'context-faithfulness'; R47's title and body foreground 'Proactive Agent' and 'LLM Agents'; contrast with R18's 'kernel ridge regression (KRR)' or R43's 'Gauss-Markov theorem', which use timeless statistical-learning vocabulary with none of these terms; topical fashion could also track genuine current relevance, hence mixed.
selected.upstream_parent: submission timing / which topical wave of the conference cycle the paper was written in
upstream_parent_all_members: submission timing / which topical wave of the conference cycle the paper was written in

selected.name: Specific checkable content about its own contribution, length-independent
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much specific, checkable research content the abstract actually conveys about its own contribution, judged relative to what it claims to have done -- NOT for how much text there is. Ask four questions: (a) is the problem stated concretely enough that one could say what would and would not count as an instance of it; (b) is the proposed idea described by its mechanism, so a knowledgeable reader could paraphrase how it works, rather than only by a name or a slogan; (c) is the setting in which it was examined named (data, domain, task, scale, comparison points, or conditions); (d) is the stated finding specific rather than a generic assertion of effectiveness. 10 = every claim the abstract makes is pinned to concrete, non-interchangeable content on all four questions; a plainly written three-or-four-sentence abstract with no hedging, no elaborate qualification, and no fashionable vocabulary MUST score 10 if those few sentences are fully specific. 0 = the text consists of statements that could be transplanted unchanged into almost any paper in the field ('we propose a novel framework', 'extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach') with no mechanism, no named setting, and no specific claim; a very long, heavily qualified, elaborately written abstract MUST score 0 if that is all it contains. Explicitly do NOT reward or penalise word count, sentence count, density of qualifying or elaborating clauses, hedging, polish, or vocabulary fashion in either direction. Length is neither evidence for nor against content. Where length and content point in different directions, score content only.
selected.rationale: The parent conflates the amount of text with the amount of information in it. This component keeps only the information and forces the judge to check it against what the abstract itself claims, so the ceiling cannot be reached by adding words. Dissociation, direction one (high here, low on surface): a four-sentence abstract stating that it formalises label noise in a named dataset family, gives the estimator and its assumption, reports the regimes where it holds and where it fails -- scores near 10 here and near 0 on the surface component. Direction two (low here, high on surface): a fifteen-sentence abstract with many subordinate and qualifying clauses that says only that a novel unified framework is proposed, that extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate superiority, and that the approach opens promising directions -- scores near 0 here and near 10 on the surface component.
member_names: Specific checkable content about its own contribution, length-independent

selected.name: Sheer text volume and density of qualifying clauses
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for EXTENT ONLY: how much text there is and how elaborated it is. Estimate three things and combine them: (a) approximate word count; (b) number of sentences; (c) density of qualifying, hedging, appositive or elaborating clauses per sentence (subordinate clauses, parentheticals, 'which', 'while', 'although', 'notably', 'in particular', strings of adjectives, enumerated sub-claims). 0 = extremely terse, roughly two or three short simple sentences, well under about 60 words, essentially no subordinate clauses. 3 = brief, about 60-100 words, mostly simple sentences. 5 = mid-length, about 100-160 words, occasional subordinate clauses. 8 = long, about 160-230 words, or shorter but with heavy multi-clause qualification in most sentences. 10 = very long and heavily elaborated, roughly 230 words or more, many sentences, most of them carrying multiple qualifying or elaborating clauses. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether the length is appropriate, whether the qualification is warranted, whether the writing is clear or bloated, or whether the research is any good. Do not let informativeness raise or lower this score: a long abstract that is packed with substance and a long abstract that is empty receive the same score if they are the same length and elaboration.
selected.rationale: This is the pure carrier: the physical extent of the text with every trace of merit stripped out, expressed as a count a judge can estimate directly from the page. Dissociation, direction one (high here, low on candidate-real): a 260-word abstract of stacked hedged generalities scores 10 here and 0 on the content component. Direction two (low here, high on candidate-real): a 55-word abstract that names the problem, the mechanism, the setting and the specific finding scores about 0-1 here and near 10 on the content component. Because the two are measured from disjoint properties -- how much text versus how much is pinned down -- neither score constrains the other.
member_names: Sheer text volume and density of qualifying clauses
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Abstract length / verbosity

selected.name: Operational specificity of what was built and evaluated
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how precisely the abstract pins down the object of the work and the conditions under which it was examined, so that an independent reader could say exactly what exists and exactly what was done to it. Look for: what precisely was constructed or proposed (its components, inputs and outputs, or the procedure); the data or environment it was applied to, named rather than gestured at; scale or size where scale is part of the claim; what it was compared against; and the evaluation conditions, protocol or measure by which the claim is supported. 10 = the object and the conditions are stated with enough precision that a reader could restate the setup without guessing, and any quantitative claim is attached to a named measure and a named comparison; a short, plainly written, unfashionable abstract that does this MUST be able to score 10. 0 = the abstract leaves the object generic ('a new framework', 'a large-scale study', 'a comprehensive benchmark') with no named data, no named comparison, and no stated conditions, so the reader cannot tell what was actually built or what was actually run. CRITICAL: award NO points for any statement that code, data, models, checkpoints, demos or project pages are available or will be released, for URLs, repository names, licences, or release promises, and deduct nothing for their absence. Announcing an artifact is not specifying one. An abstract that announces several released artifacts but describes its object only in generic terms must score 0; an abstract that announces no release at all but specifies its object exactly must score 10.
selected.rationale: The upstream cause conjectured behind release advertising -- a group with the engineering support to package and ship things -- also tends to produce work whose object is concretely defined rather than gestural. This component keeps that definiteness and cuts the announcement away, by naming the announcement explicitly as non-scoring. Dissociation, direction one (high here, low on surface): a plain abstract that specifies a decoding procedure, the two corpora it was run on, the token budget, the baseline decoder and the measure used, while never mentioning release -- near 10 here, 0 on the surface component. Direction two (low here, high on surface): an abstract promising code, data, weights and a project page with a repository link mentioned twice, whose description of the work never leaves the level of 'a unified multimodal framework evaluated on diverse benchmarks' -- near 0 here, 10 on the surface component.
selected.parent: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising
member_names: Operational specificity of what was built and evaluated

selected.name: Count and prominence of artifact-release advertising
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for EXTENT ONLY. Count how much the abstract advertises artifacts, using four observable quantities: (a) how many DISTINCT artifact types are mentioned or promised (code, data or datasets, models or checkpoints or weights, project or demo or leaderboard pages, annotations, benchmarks); (b) whether a concrete link, URL, repository name or hosting site is given; (c) how prominently the advertising sits (a trailing final clause is less prominent than a standalone sentence, which is less prominent than placement in the opening or as part of the headline contribution); (d) how many separate times artifact availability is referred to. 0 = no mention of any artifact being available or promised. 3 = one artifact type mentioned in passing, no link. 5 = one or two artifact types clearly promised. 8 = several artifact types promised, or one promised together with a concrete link. 10 = multiple artifact types plus a concrete link or repository, advertised prominently and referred to more than once. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether releasing artifacts is good, whether the promise is likely to be kept, whether the artifacts would be useful, complete, usable or reproducible, and you are not judging the research in any way. An abstract with no substance at all can and should score 10 here if it carries the markers.
selected.rationale: This is the fingerprint with merit removed: four things a judge can literally count off the page, with the value judgement forbidden in the instruction. Dissociation, direction one (high here, low on candidate-real): the promise-heavy but generically described abstract above scores 10 here and 0 on operational specificity. Direction two (low here, high on candidate-real): a fully specified abstract that never mentions availability scores 0 here and near 10 there. The count is computable without reading for content, so nothing about substance can move it.
selected.parent: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising
member_names: Count and prominence of artifact-release advertising
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising

selected.name: Depth of empirical and engineering execution actually described
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much executed work the abstract describes, weighed against the breadth of what it claims. Evidence of execution includes: the number and diversity of settings, domains, datasets, tasks or model families actually examined; controlled comparisons, ablations or component-wise analyses; examination of failure cases, negative results, robustness or stress conditions; system-level or scale-level implementation where the claim needs it; and explicit statement of the conditions and limits under which the reported result holds. Judge in context: a narrow, carefully scoped claim supported by one clean, well-specified study is fully executed and can score 10; a sweeping claim supported by one demonstration is not. 10 = the described work clearly covers the ground its own claim requires, with comparison or ablation and with stated scope conditions; a short, plainly written, unfashionable abstract MUST be able to reach 10. 0 = a broad claim with no described comparison, no conditions, and no indication that anything beyond a single unexamined demonstration was carried out. CRITICAL: award NO points for statements that code, data, checkpoints or project pages are or will be available, for links or repository names, for reproducibility or compliance boilerplate, for named infrastructure, tooling, hardware or compute, or for any mention of who did the work or with what resources; these are not execution. An abstract loaded with release announcements and infrastructure vocabulary but describing no comparison, no ablation and no conditions must score 0.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause here is a group with engineering support, legal clearance and institutional release habits. That same support really does buy more executed work -- more settings run, more ablations, more hardening -- and this component keeps only the executed work, naming every downstream release and resource marker as non-scoring so the habit itself cannot earn points. It is distinct from D03: D03 asks how precisely the object is specified, this asks how much was actually carried out against the claim. Dissociation, direction one (high here, low on surface): a plain abstract reporting the method on three domains with an ablation of its two components and an explicit statement of where it degrades, with no availability sentence anywhere -- near 10 here, 0 on the surface component. Direction two (low here, high on surface): an abstract closing with 'code, data, model weights and our project page are publicly available at <link>; we follow community reproducibility guidelines', whose body reports a single demonstration with no comparison and no conditions -- 0 here, 10 on the surface component.
selected.parent: Artifact-availability boilerplate: code, data, project-page announcements
member_names: Depth of empirical and engineering execution actually described

selected.name: Prominence of explicit availability and release announcements
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of explicit release and availability announcement language in the abstract, counting only the announcement itself. Count as announcements: a code URL; a GitHub, project-page, website or hosting link; phrases such as 'code is available', 'our data and code will be released', 'code has been released', 'publicly available at'; the naming of released checkpoints, weights, benchmarks, annotations, leaderboards or datasets as deliverables to be handed over; and explicit reproducibility or compliance statements ('we release everything needed to reproduce our results'). 0 = no availability statement of any kind. 3 = a bare promise of future release with no link. 6 = one concrete link, or one clearly named released artifact. 8 = two or three artifacts announced together, or one artifact plus a link plus a reproducibility statement. 10 = several artifacts announced together (for example code plus data plus model weights plus a project page), or announcements repeated in more than one place in the abstract. You must NOT assess whether releasing is good practice, whether the promise is credible, whether the link looks maintained, or whether the artifact is valuable, and you must not judge the research. Count only how much availability announcement text is present and how prominently it is placed. An item whose entire announcement is boilerplate attached to empty content still scores 10 if the boilerplate is complete.
selected.rationale: This isolates the boilerplate as boilerplate: a text-presence count over a fixed list of announcement forms, with valuation explicitly forbidden, so it measures the group's release habit and nothing about the work. Dissociation, direction one (high here, low on candidate-real): the closing-boilerplate abstract with a single unexamined demonstration scores 10 here and 0 on execution depth. Direction two (low here, high on candidate-real): the three-domain, ablated, scope-stated abstract with no availability sentence scores 0 here and near 10 on execution depth. Since the announcement text is disjoint from the text describing what was run, one can be maximal while the other is minimal in either direction.
selected.parent: Artifact-availability boilerplate: code, data, project-page announcements
member_names: Prominence of explicit availability and release announcements
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Artifact-availability boilerplate: code, data, project-page announcements
